Q1: 2-Ethoxynaphthalene presents a mixed hazard profile, with known significant environmental hazards (Tier 1) and potential dermal and eye hazards identified through an expanded perspective (Tier 2). However, a substantial portion of its hazard profile remains data deficient, specifically for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR), inhalation hazards (IHL), and organ and systemic hazards (OGN). Oral and endocrine disruption hazards are currently classified as low to moderate (Tier 3).
Q2: 2-Ethoxynaphthalene is not currently listed on any specified "Lists of Concern." Q3: 2-Ethoxynaphthalene appears to be moderately well-characterized in terms of its chemical identity, possessing a defined molecular formula (C12H12O) and substance class as a small molecule, and it is not identified as a UVCB.
